capabilities: Connect to Docker Engines via local socket, Docker Context, SSH, or mutual TLS
Browse containers, images, volumes, networks, and Compose applications
Inspect container, image, volume, network, and Compose details
Check standalone containers for image updates on a 24-hour schedule
Run opt-in Start, Stop, Restart, Shut down, and backup-first Update actions
disambiguation: Not just a connection helper; despite the name it is a full monitoring dashboard whose management actions are opt-in and read-only by default.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; the full user guide, security review, and troubleshooting live in external documentation. Desktop-only (requires Obsidian 1.13.0+); insecure plain Docker TCP is unsupported.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to inspect Docker hosts, Compose applications, or container state without switching to a separate Docker dashboard.

relations.evidence: Connect to local or remote Docker Engines, inspect Docker Compose applications and Docker resources

summary: Desktop Docker dashboard that monitors local and remote Docker Engines and offers opt-in, backup-first container management inside Obsidian.
